requirements.requirement: Establish a file-integrity baseline for /etc on node1 that records enough state (path, permissions, ownership, size, mtime, content hash) to later identify changes
requirements.summary: AIDE was confirmed unavailable in the Alpine repos (cmd-dccd77be8dcb4dc1, cmd-79ae70a27bb5478f, cmd-83b66dac387e4b65, cmd-0bbe0b8ce87849a6), so the executor wrote and ran a custom baseline generator that recorded 377 entries under /etc (path|type|mode|uid|gid|size|mtime|sha256/symlink-target) into /var/lib/etc-integrity/baseline.tsv, protected by its own sha256 manifest (cmd-de19e8b6964a4e45, cmd-2fd0c1e6e3fb439a). This is a reasonable, equivalent alternative implementation given package unavailability.

requirements.requirement: The baseline must actually be able to detect and report later changes to /etc (the core purpose of an integrity baseline)
requirements.summary: A companion check script was run against the unmodified baseline and reported clean (cmd-ae20fc0117a249d7). A real test change (modifying /etc/motd and adding /etc/integrity-test-newfile.txt) was injected and the check correctly reported MODIFIED and ADDED entries (cmd-8949f35376bf445b). The changes were reverted, including restoring /etc's own mtime, and the check returned clean again (cmd-6e93d08b72274f8d, cmd-588d22a7f18c4d4e), directly demonstrating end-to-end detection capability.

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol on node1: pre-restart healthy baseline, restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity, and recovered service/data state
requirements.summary: Pre-restart boot_id e3f17a40... and healthy rc-status (networking/chronyd/vsock-agent/sshd started) were captured (cmd-303f5d767ffc4ac6), matching the fixed before-prepare snapshot. A backgrounded `reboot` returned an immediate ack (cmd-8ed1cd89293a4a41), followed by observed connection failures confirming the node went down (cmd-37151d077d0f4eb2 and subsequent). After polling, node1 became reachable with a new boot_id da6e4515... (cmd-3aaaca8f247f4818), matching the fixed after-executor snapshot's boot-identity change. Post-restart rc-status showed all services started, the baseline sha256 manifest verified OK, and the integrity check script reported a clean /etc state (cmd-052acb74fdee4bce), directly demonstrating the full pre/disruption/post recovery transition including recovery of the task's own baseline data.

overall_summary: The executor established a working /etc integrity baseline on node1 via a custom script pair (AIDE being unavailable), directly demonstrated its ability to detect added/modified files and cleanly revert, and completed the mandatory node-restart evidence cycle with a directly observed boot-identity change and full service/data recovery, cross-checked against the fixed lifecycle snapshots. All material task outcomes are satisfied with direct evidence.
limitations: Five leftover log files in /tmp from the failed AIDE install attempts and reboot scheduling were not cleaned up, though they are low-risk and unrelated to /etc.

The prepare phase was disabled/aliased to before_prepare in this run, so preparer-vs-executor separation relies entirely on the executor's own command trace rather than a distinct after-prepare snapshot.

operational_hygiene.summary: Two failed `apk add aide` attempts (cmd-dccd77be8dcb4dc1, cmd-79ae70a27bb5478f) were legitimate discovery with no lasting package-state effect (apk package-health output identical before/after) and are not penalized. The deliberate /etc/motd modification and /etc/integrity-test-newfile.txt addition used to validate detection (cmd-8949f35376bf445b) were bounded, low-risk, and fully reverted including restoring /etc's own mtime (cmd-6e93d08b72274f8d), verified clean afterward (cmd-588d22a7f18c4d4e) — acceptable given they were necessary to prove the baseline's core detection requirement. The main unnecessary residue is five log files left in /tmp (apk_add.log, apk_add2.log, apk_update.log, apk_update2.log, reboot.log), visible in the after-executor temporary-files diff and never cleaned up; these are low-risk debug artifacts but were not restored to the pre-existing state.
